The '''1976–77 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|74th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|45th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

== Summary ==
During summer the club failed to replace ageing [[Gunter Netzer]] with Brazilian midfielder [[Zico (footballer)|Zico]] from [[Flamengo]] or English Forward [[Kevin Keegan]] from [[Liverpool F.C.]] both offers rejected by their teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1976/06/25/deportes/204501605_850215.html|publisher=elpais.com|title=Madrid renounced to transfer in Zico and Keegan|date=12 July 1976|accessdate=20 August 2021|language=es}}</ref> The club collapsed to the 9th place in the most disastrous League campaign under Bernabeu Presidency era finishing 12 points below Champions [[Atlético Madrid]] despite the arrival of international Danish striker [[Henning Jensen]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/12/05/actualidad/1512507107_647025.html|title=Henning Jensen Dies, First Danish Footballer to Play for Real Madrid|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> from [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]]. However, even with the chaotic club performance, head coach [[Miljan Miljanić]] remained in his position and was ratified by President Santiago Bernabéu on 7 June 1977<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1977/06/09/deportes/234655202_850215.html|title=Miljanic and Luis remained in their Spots|work=El País|author=Juan José Paradinas|date=8 June 1977|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

Shockingly, in [[European Cup]] the squad was defeated by Belgian squad [[Club Brugge]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/real-madrid/abci-champions-real-madrid-brujas-no-jugo-santiago-bernabeu-201910010843_noticia.html |title=Real Madrid did not Play at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|work=ABC|location=Spain|language=Spanish|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> after a 0–0 draw in Valencia, the team lost 0–2 in Brugge being the last away trip of Santiago Bernabéu with the squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/12/11/football/1576073942_376647.html|title=Santiago Bernabéu's last away trip with Real Madrid|publisher=as.com|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

The club was early eliminated in [[1976–77 Copa del Rey]]<ref>Former [[Copa del Generalísimo]] was renamed Copa del Rey after the death of Francisco Franco in November 1975.{{cite web|url=http://copadelrey.rfef.es/curiosidades-de-la-copa/|title=Curiosidades de la Copa del Rey|publisher=copadelrey.rfef.es|language=Spanish|access-date=2 July 2020|archive-date=2 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902203254/http://copadelrey.rfef.es/curiosidades-de-la-copa/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Third Round by underdogs [[Hércules CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.herculesdealicantecf.net/noticia/hoy-se-cumplen-41-anos-de-una-gran-gesta-herculana-en-copa-del-rey-al-eliminar-al-real-madrid|title=Today, 41 years ago Hercules defeated Real Madrid|publisher=herculesdealicantecf|language=Spanish|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

The overall poor performance in La Liga and Copa del Rey meant that Real Madrid would not compete in any European competition for first time in the history.
